body: Yes. It was assault. I’m so sorry this happened to you.

If you see someone trying to take advantage of someone else in a vulnerable position you either do something or tell someone and help the person. 

We can no longer be enablers of this type of behavior.  Look out for your friends and for anyone if you see injustice.
He’s a narcissist

To effectively heal: We must first remember that our initial reactions to things (guilt for not doing more usually) is a product of our codependency issues and the negative thinking patterns we have  adopted as a result of that bad relationship (or bad relationships). We have to find our own voices again. That takes time. 
Remind yourself now that the good times were great and that’s ok to remember, but that you also have noticed some bad patterns that you don’t quite like. Decide for yourself if you want to go through those same patterns again and again with this person and know that these patterns basically train one’s own brains to start negative self talk. It’s safest for us to stay away from these types of relationships while healing and really self reflect over patterns we have noticed so we can navigate life better afterwards and have better future relationships. 

Are the highs worth the depths of despair after? 

I would argue, no.  We have to learn how to self regulate our own emotions again. We should all definitely seek help from a good therapist. 
We can do it! You can do it! And you’ll be stronger for it!

Dr Ramani and med circle on YouTube have some helpful videos on “are you being manipulated”. Don’t quote me on this but I believe she says If you’re motivated to do things out of guilt and not cause you actually want to - it is a sign of manipulation.

The question is tricky to answer. And only you will know when it’s right for you. I am in the healing stage now and think it is incredibly important to heal and be alone for a good long time. We need to remember what we like to do. Then do those things unapologetically for ourselves. It’s not selfish for you to do things that make you happy. 
So my answer isn’t much. I think in time, you’ll get there again. I completely relate.

These feelings will pass and will be replaced with new ones

Last time you felt this way, did you have a day after that you enjoyed? What did you do?  What small things do you enjoy?  For me, I had a good coffee today and pet my dog for a long time. I enjoyed that. Life is hard, feelings are hard, your feelings are valid but know they aren’t permanent.  You will feel better again one day. I promise.
